beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That makes the conflict harder than a simple contest against obviously evil rulers.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Chamber of Measure rarely needs to say that a birth is forbidden.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Instead, an application can be deferred into a future that keeps receding.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Sava understands why a finite habitat cannot ignore population and food.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: She also encounters families for whom the calculation becomes an intimate loss.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An official form turns several humanlike needs into one administrative decision.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Even mercy must find a category that the system will accept.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The chapter makes a resource problem legible without making its cruelty disappear.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Oru approaches the same civilization through the things that require repair.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A failing pipe is a material problem before it becomes an acceptable statistic.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Sava worries about what breaks when every official overrules the model.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Oru worries about what breaks when nobody questions its picture.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Their disagreement stays inside a relationship built on affection and shared responsibilities.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Neither perspective can sustain the whole world alone, which gives their conversations tension.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Reading lets you stay with that tension longer than a slogan would allow.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Beyond the capital, Vaor challenges the centre's account of the Belt.
